subject: Post-discovery: runway deployment topology & SLO mapping — workshop windows
snippet: Proposing 60-minute technical deep-dive to map deployment topology and SLOs; proposing time slots and asking for SRE attendance.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@helios.ai>, platform-eng@helios.ai
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery: runway deployment topology & SLO mapping — workshop windows

Hi Jordan / Helios platform team,

Thanks again for the discovery call yesterday — really helpful context. As a next step we'd like to run a 60-minute technical deep-dive to walk through:
- proposed deployment topology (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- networking and data-residency constraints
- latency & throughput SLOs and how those map to instance sizing / batching
- any compliance controls you need (audit logs, KMS)

Goal: produce a short mutual action plan and a recommended instance/topology sketch we can hand off to your SREs.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue Aug 24, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Tue Aug 24, 15:00–16:00 PT
- Wed Aug 25, 08:00–09:00 PT

If none of these work, share a couple of 1-hour windows that do. Please include any teammates from SRE, infra, or security who should join. I’ve attached a one-page agenda and a rough topology diagram we plan to review.

Attaching: redwood-deep-dive-agenda-v1.pdf (agenda), helm-network-topology.png (diagram stub)

Thanks — I’ll create a calendar invite once we lock a slot.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

Ben — thanks, the agenda looks good. Quick note: our infra lead (outages) has a standing all-hands Tue 10am PT so that slot won't work for us.

We prefer Tue Aug 24 at 15:00 PT if that suits your team. A couple of prep questions to help our SREs prep:
- Do you need a sample traffic profile (qps + typical prompt length) ahead of time?
- Can you confirm whether Redwood’s private deployment supports a customer-controlled data egress rule (we need traffic to stay within our VPC)?
- Our latency target is 95th percentile < 250ms for inference under p95 load; is that realistic for your recommended topology?

I’ll loop in platform-eng@helios.ai to add any additional attendees.

Thanks,
Jordan Reed

Jordan — 15:00 PT on Tue Aug 24 works for our team. I’ll send a calendar invite for a 60-minute slot for 15:00–16:00 PT and include dial-in + shared Drive link.

Quick answers to your prep questions so SREs can prep:
- Sample traffic profile: yes, please share a short CSV with typical qps and average prompt length (tokens). If you prefer, send peak-minute qps and 95th percentile prompt lengths and we’ll model capacity sizing.
- Private deployment and egress: Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC peering and control-plane-in-network options; we can enforce egress rules so traffic stays inside your VPC. We’ll bring a network diagram to the workshop.
- 95p < 250ms: achievable depending on prompt length and quantization choices. We'll run a quick sizing exercise in the session. For benchmarking reference, please mention the typical max sequence length you expect.

Agenda (attached) — we'll cover sizing, topology options, operational controls, and a short appendix on cost tradeoffs and quantization recommendations.

Soojin — can you bring the deployment examples (multi-region failover + KV-cache layout) and the small script we use for p95 estimation? Marissa, can you include the canonical runbook link in the invite?

Thanks — invite incoming.

Ben
